Surah Ghafir, also called al-Mu'min [Meccan, except verses 56 and 57, which are Medinan; its verses number 85]. It was revealed after az-Zumar.

﴿Ha-Mim﴾. Allah knows best what He means by it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 2:

﴿The revelation of the Book﴾ (the Qur'an) is the subject (mubtada'), and ﴿from Allah﴾ is its predicate (khabar); ﴿the Mighty﴾ in His dominion, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾ of His creation.

ـ(Ghafir al-dhanb) forgiver of sin, for the believers; (wa qabil al-tawb) and acceptor of repentance, from them; (tawb is a verbal noun, masdar); (shadid al-iqab) severe in punishment, for the disbelievers; i.e., (ʿiqab is) intensified (mushaddada).

(Dhi al-tawl) possessor of bounty, i.e., wide favour. He is described constantly with all these attributes, so the idafa (genitive construction) of the participles derived from them is definite, as is the last one.

(La ilaha illa Huwa) "There is no god but Him" (ilayhi al-masir) "to Him is the return," i.e., the place of return.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 4:

﴿None dispute concerning the signs of Allah﴾ the Qur'an ﴿except those who disbelieve﴾ from among the people of Makkah. ﴿So do not be deceived by their going back and forth throughout the land﴾ moving about safely for trade and livelihood, for their end is the Fire.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 5:

﴿Before them the people of Noah denied, and the factions after them did likewise.﴾ Such as ʿAd, Thamud and others. ﴿And every nation schemed against their messenger to seize him﴾ to kill him. ﴿And they argued with falsehood in order to refute﴾ to remove ﴿thereby the truth. So I seized them﴾ with punishment ﴿so how was My punishment﴾ upon them? That is, it fell in its proper place.

And thus ﴿the word of your Lord has been fulfilled﴾, i.e. ﴿"I will surely fill Hell with jinn and humankind"﴾ ... ﴿the verse﴾, ﴿against those who disbelieved, that they are the companions of the Fire﴾. ﴿That they are the companions of the Fire﴾ is a *badal* (substitution, i.e. apposition) for ﴿the word﴾ (كَلِمَة).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 7:

﴿Those who bear the Throne﴾ is a subject (mubtada'). ﴿And those around it﴾ is conjoined to it (ma'tuf). ﴿Glorify﴾ is its predicate (khabar). ﴿With the praise of their Lord﴾ [meaning] while accompanied by praise, i.e., they say: "Glory be to Allah, and with His praise." ﴿And believe in Him﴾ [exalted is He] with their insight, i.e., they affirm His oneness (wahdaniyyah). ﴿And ask forgiveness for those who believed﴾ saying: ﴿"Our Lord, You encompass all things in mercy and knowledge"﴾, i.e., Your mercy has encompassed everything and Your knowledge has encompassed everything. ﴿So forgive those who repent﴾ from shirk ﴿and follow Your way﴾, the religion of Islam, ﴿and protect them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire﴾, i.e., the Fire.

﴿Our Lord, and admit them to the Gardens of Eden﴾ (abode), ﴿which You promised them, and those who were righteous﴾ is conjoined (ʿuṭifa, grammatically "coordinated") with the pronoun in ﴿وأَدْخِلْهُمْ﴾ or in ﴿وعَدْتهمْ﴾, ﴿among their fathers, their spouses, and their descendants. Indeed You, You are the Almighty, the All-Wise﴾ in His doing.
﴿And protect them from evil deeds﴾, meaning from its punishment. ﴿And whomever You protect from evil deeds on that Day﴾, meaning the Day of Resurrection.

Verily, those who disbelieved will be called out to [by the angels], and they will loathe themselves upon entering the Fire. ﴿Surely God's loathing of you﴾ [is greater] ﴿than your loathing of yourselves, when you were called﴾ to faith in the world.

﴿They will say: "Our Lord, You caused us to die twice and You gave us life twice."﴾ *Imatatayn* (إماتَتَيْنِ, two instances of causing to die) and *ihya'atayn* (إحْياءَتَيْنِ, two instances of giving life). They were given life twice because they were *nutaf* (نُطَف, drops of seminal fluid), which are dead, so they were given life, then caused to die, then given life again for the resurrection (*lil-ba'th*, for the Resurrection).

﴿So we have confessed our sins﴾, meaning our disbelief in the Resurrection. ﴿Is there any way to go out﴾, meaning out of the Fire, and return to the world so that we may obey our Lord? ﴿Any way?﴾, meaning any path? Their answer is: No.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 12:

﴿That⁠﴾ i.e., the punishment you are in, ﴿because﴾ i.e., because of the fact that, in the world, ﴿when Allah alone was invoked, you disbelieved﴾ in His oneness, ﴿but when partners were associated with Him﴾ i.e., were made to be His partners, ﴿you believed﴾ you affirmed the association, ﴿so judgment﴾ regarding your punishment ﴿belongs to Allah, the Most High﴾ over His creation, ﴿the Great﴾ the Magnificent.

He it is who shows you His signs (﴿آياته﴾ — i.e., the proofs of His oneness), and sends down for you provision (﴿رِزْقًا﴾) from the sky, by way of rain. None takes heed (﴿يَتَذَكَّر﴾ — i.e., is admonished) except him who turns back (﴿يُنِيب﴾ — i.e., returns from polytheism).
﴿So call upon Allah﴾, i.e., worship Him, ﴿sincerely devoting religion to Him﴾, free from polytheism, ﴿even if the disbelievers dislike it﴾, i.e., your sincerity toward Him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 15:

﴿Rafi' al-darajat﴾ (Exalted in degrees): i.e., Allah is great in attributes; or He raises the degrees of the believers in Paradise. ﴿Dhu al-'Arsh﴾ (Lord of the Throne): its Creator. ﴿Yulqi al-Ruh﴾ (He sends down the revelation, al-ruh): ﴿min amrihi﴾ (by His command), i.e., His word, ﴿'ala man yasha'u min 'ibadihi﴾ (upon whomever He wills of His servants), ﴿li-yundhira﴾ (so that he may warn), i.e., frighten the people to whom it is sent, ﴿yawm al-talaq﴾ (the Day of Encounter), with the letter ya' omitted or retained in reading: the Day of Resurrection, because of the meeting (talaqi) of the people of the heavens and the earth, the worshipper and the worshipped, and the oppressor and the oppressed in it.

On the Day they will come forth (﴿يَوْم هُمْ بارِزُونَ﴾), coming out of their graves, ﴿nothing about them will be hidden from God﴾. ﴿"Whose is the dominion today?"﴾ He, exalted is He, says it and answers Himself: ﴿"To God, the One, the Subduer."﴾ That is, to His creation.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 40, verse 17:

﴿Today every soul will be recompensed for what it has earned. There is no injustice today. Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning.﴾ He will call all creation to account in the span of half a day from the days of this world, according to a hadith to that effect.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 18:

﴿And warn them of the Imminent Day﴾ — the Day of Resurrection, from azifa al-raḥīl (it drew near), i.e., qaruba (it came close). ﴿When the hearts rise up to the throats﴾ — rising up in fear, ﴿choking﴾ — ﴿lada﴾ meaning ʿinda (at), ﴿al-ḥanājir﴾ (the throats), ﴿kāẓimīn﴾ (choking, suppressing) — filled with grief. It is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) from "the hearts"; it is treated with the masculine plural ending (yāʾ and nūn) in accordance with the treatment of its owners. ﴿The wrongdoers will have no intimate friend﴾ — ḥamīm, meaning a beloved, ﴿nor an intercessor who will be obeyed﴾ — there is no implied contrast (mafhūm) in the descriptive phrase, since they have no intercessor at all. ﴿So we have no intercessors﴾ — the first part carries an implied contrast (mafhūm) based on their supposition that they have intercessors; that is, even if they were to intercede hypothetically, they would not be accepted.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 19:

﴿He knows﴾, that is, Allah, ﴿the treachery of the eyes﴾ by their stealthily glancing at what is forbidden, ﴿and what the breasts conceal﴾, that is, the hearts.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 20:

﴿Allah judges with truth, while those whom they invoke besides Him﴾ worship, i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah, with the verb in the yā' and the tā' forms, ﴿besides Him﴾, and they are the idols, ﴿do not judge anything.﴾ So how can they be partners with Allah? ﴿Indeed, Allah is the All-Hearing﴾ of their statements, ﴿the All-Seeing﴾ of their deeds.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 21:

﴿Have they not travelled through the land and seen how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in strength and in traces left upon the earth﴾, and in another reading, "than you" (minkum), ﴿in buildings and palaces﴾ made of factories and mansions. ﴿So Allah seized them﴾, destroyed them, ﴿for their sins, and they had no protector from Allah﴾ against His punishment.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 22:

﴿That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs⦌ with the manifest miracles.
We sent Musa with Our signs and a clear authority (sultan mubin), meaning: a plain, manifest proof.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 24:

﴿To Pharaoh, Haman and Qarun; but they said﴾ he is ﴿a lying sorcerer﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 40, verse 25:

﴿So when he brought them the truth﴾ with sincerity ﴿from Us, they said: "Kill the sons of those who believe with him, and spare their women."﴾ spare (istabqū) their women ﴿But the scheming of the disbelievers is only in error﴾ destruction.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 26:

﴿And Pharaoh said, "Leave me to kill Moses, and let him call upon his Lord. Indeed, I fear that he will change your religion or that he will cause corruption in the land."﴾ [He said this] because they were restraining him from killing him. ﴿Let him call upon his Lord﴾ so that his Lord may protect him from me. ﴿Indeed, I fear that he will change your religion﴾ from your worship of me, so that you follow him. ﴿Or that he will cause corruption in the land﴾ through killing and other things. And in another reading: "أوْ" [read as "aw"] and in another reading: "أوْ" is read with a fatha on the yā' and the hā' and a ḍamma on the dāl (i.e., "yuẓhira" becomes "yaẓhara"... ) 

Note on the readings: The text as given reads "وفِي قِراءَة: أوْ وفِي أُخْرى بِفَتْحِ الياء والهاء وضَمّ الدّال", which I have rendered above. The precise sense of the second reading is as follows: in the other reading, the verb "yuẓhira" (يُظْهِر) is read as "yaẓhara" (يَظْهَر) with a fatha on the yā' and the hā' and a ḍamma on the dāl, i.e., "yadhuhur" (يَدْهُر)... [see correction below]

Correction: The verb in the other reading is read with a fatha on the yā' and on the hā' and a ḍamma on the dāl, giving "yaẓharu"-type forms; the passage's wording refers to the reading of the verb "yaẓhara/yuẓhira" in the Arabic original, which I should not have rendered with an invented gloss. The faithful translation of the reading note is: "And in another reading: 'aw', and in another reading (the verb) with a fatha on the yā' and the hā' and a ḍamma on the dāl."
{And Moses said} to his people, when he had heard that:

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 28:

﴿And a believing man from the family of Pharaoh, who concealed his faith, said﴾. It is said: he was his cousin (ibn ʿamm).
﴿"Will you kill a man because he says: My Lord is Allah, and he has brought you clear proofs (al-bayyināt) from your Lord"﴾, i.e., because (li-ann) he says, "My Lord is Allah," and he has come to you with the manifest miracles (al-muʿjizāt al-ẓāhirāt), ﴿from your Lord. And if he is a liar, then upon him is his lie﴾, i.e., the harm of his lie. ﴿And if he is truthful, some of what he promises you will befall you﴾, of the punishment he threatens you with, swiftly. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a transgressor (musrif)﴾, a polytheist (mushrik), ﴿a liar (kadhdhāb)﴾, one who fabricates (muftarin).

O my people, the kingdom is yours today, dominant (ghalibin, a circumstantial accusative) in the land, [the land of Egypt]. Then who will help us against the might (ba's) of God, [His punishment], if we kill His friends, should it come upon us? [That is,] there is no helper for us.

Pharaoh said: "I show you only what I see" [i.e., I only advise you with what I advise myself, and that is the killing of Moses], "and I guide you only to the path of right conduct" [the path of correctness].
And the one who believed said, "O my people, indeed I fear for you a day like the day of the factions" — that is, a day of one faction after another.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 31:

﴿Like the custom of the people of Noah, and ʿĀd, and Thamūd, and those after them﴾. "Like" (mithl) is a substitute (badal) for the preceding "mithl", meaning: like the recompense of the habit of those who disbelieved before you, of their punishment in the worldly life.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 32:

﴿And O my people, indeed I fear for you the Day of Calling-Out﴾ with the yā' (الياء, the letter ya) elided (بِحَذْفِ) and with it retained (وإثباتها). That is, the Day of Resurrection, on which the calling of the people of Paradise to the people of the Fire will be frequent, and the reverse, and the calling to those of happiness (بِالسَّعادَةِ) for its people and to those of wretchedness (بِالشَّقاوَةِ) for its people, and other than that.
ﷻ﴿The Day you will turn your backs, fleeing﴾ away from the place of reckoning toward the Fire, ﴿you will have no protector from God﴾ i.e., from His punishment, ﴿none to shield you﴾, preventing it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 34:

﴿And certainly Joseph came to you before with clear proofs﴾ i.e., before Moses. He is Joseph son of Jacob, according to the opinion of ʿAmmar, [the time being] up to the time of Moses; or Joseph son of Ibrahim son of Joseph son of Jacob, according to another opinion. ﴿With clear proofs﴾ with the manifest miracles. ﴿But you continued in doubt about what he brought you, until, when he perished, you said﴾ without any proof: ﴿Allah will not send after him any messenger﴾ i.e., you will continue to disbelieve in Joseph and others. ﴿Thus﴾ i.e., like your misguidance, ﴿Allah leads astray whoever is a transgressor﴾ a polytheist ﴿and a doubter﴾ one who is in doubt about what the clear proofs testify to.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 40, verse 35:

﴿Those who dispute concerning the signs of God﴾ — His miracles; (alladhina) is the subject (mubtada'). ﴿without any authority﴾ — without proof. ﴿having come to them﴾. ﴿Great is their hatred﴾ — their disputing; (kabura) is the predicate (khabar) of the subject. ﴿in the sight of God and in the sight of those who believe﴾. ﴿Thus﴾ — like their misguidance. ﴿God seals﴾ — He stamps (yatba') — ﴿with misguidance﴾. ﴿upon every heart that is arrogant and tyrannical﴾ — with the tanwin on qalb and without it; and whenever the heart is arrogant, its owner is arrogant, and vice versa. Both readings (kull) apply to the generality of misguidance, the whole heart, not to the generality of the heart.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 36:

﴿And Pharaoh said: "O Haman, build for me a lofty tower"﴾ a tall building.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 37:

﴿Asbab al-samawat﴾ (the ways of the heavens) — its paths that lead to them. ﴿Fa-attali'a﴾ — with the raised vowel, as a conjunction with "ablugh" (I may reach), and with the accusative vowel, as an answer following "la'alli" (so that I may). ﴿Ila ilahi Musa, wa-innI la-azunnuhu﴾ — that is, Musa — ﴿kadhiban﴾ (a liar) in claiming that He has a god other than me. Pharaoh said that as a deception. ﴿Wa-kadhalika zuyyina li-Fir'awna su'u 'amalihi wa-suddda 'ani al-sabil﴾ — the path of guidance — with the sad vowelled with fatha and with damma. ﴿Wa-ma kayd Fir'awna illa fi tabab﴾ — loss (khasar).

And the one who believed said, "O my people, follow me; I will guide you to the path of right conduct." (Qur'an 40:38)

Recited with the ya' (ي) both affirmed and omitted: ﴿أهْدِكُمْ﴾ ("I will guide you") and ﴿سَبِيل الرَّشاد﴾ ("the path of right conduct") — this has already been explained earlier.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 39:

﴿O my people, indeed this worldly life is but a provision﴾ an enjoyment that will pass away.

﴿Whoever does an evil deed will not be recompensed except with its like, and whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while being a believer, those will enter Paradise, where they will be provided for without reckoning.﴾

(Read with a *ḍamma* on the *yāʾ* and a *fatḥa* on the *khāʾ* in the verb *yudkhalūna* ("they are made to enter"), and vice versa, i.e. *yadkhulūna* ("they enter").) ﴿They will be provided for therein without account﴾: abundant provision, without any consequence or reckoning.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 42:

﴿You call me to disbelieve in Allah and to associate with Him that of which I have no knowledge, while I call you to the Mighty (al-'Aziz), the One who prevails over His affair, the Oft-Forgiving (al-Ghaffar) to whoever repents.﴾

﴿Truly﴾ ﴿that what you call me to﴾ [is worship of Him], ﴿has no call﴾, i.e., no answering of a call, ﴿in this world or in the Hereafter﴾, ﴿and that our return﴾, our going back, ﴿is to God﴾, ﴿and that the transgressors﴾ are the disbelievers.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on 40:44

﴿Then you will remember﴾ what I say to you when you witness the punishment, ﴿and I entrust my affair to Allah. Indeed, Allah is Seeing of the servants.﴾ He said this when they threatened him for opposing their religion.

﴿So Allah protected him from the evil consequences of what they plotted﴾ against him, namely the killing, ﴿and there befell﴾ came down upon ﴿the people of Pharaoh﴾, his people with him, ﴿the worst torment﴾, which was drowning.

Then, [they are] the Fire; they are exposed to it: they are burned by it, ﴿morning and evening﴾, i.e., at dawn and at dusk. ﴿And on the Day the Hour is established﴾, it is said: ﴿Admit the people of Pharaoh into the most severe punishment﴾: an imperative addressed to the angels. In another reading, with a fatḥah on the hamzah and a kasrah on the khā' (ādkhilū read as adkhilū, i.e., "Cause to enter"), the words ﴿people of Pharaoh﴾ are in the vocative: O ﴿most severe punishment﴾, namely the punishment of Jahannam.

﴿And﴾ ﴿when they dispute﴾ — the disbelievers dispute ﴿in the Fire, and the weak will say to those who were arrogant: "Indeed, we were ﴾ ﴿followers [ tabaʿan ] of you"﴾. [Tabaʿan] is the plural of [tābiʿ] (follower). ﴿Will you then be ones who avert﴾ — repelling ﴿from us a portion﴾ — of the punishment?
﴿Those who were arrogant will say: Indeed, we are all in it. Indeed, Allah has judged between the servants.﴾ So He admitted the believers into Paradise and the disbelievers into the Fire.
Those in the Fire will say to the keepers of Hell, "Call upon your Lord, that He may lighten for us a day [of the punishment]," that is, "a day's worth" (of punishment).

They (the guardians of Hell) say, mockingly: ﴿Did not your messengers come to you with clear proofs?﴾ That is, with the evident miracles. ﴿They said, "Yes."﴾ That is, so they disbelieved in them. ﴿They (the guardians) said, "Then call [upon Him yourselves]"﴾, for we do not intercede for the disbelievers. ﴿But the supplication of the disbelievers is nothing but in error﴾, that is, in vain, coming to nothing.

Indeed, We shall surely help Our messengers and those who believe, in the life of this world and on the Day when the witnesses stand up (to testify).

"Al-ashhad" is the plural of "shahid" (witness), and they are the angels, who testify for the messengers that they conveyed (the message), and against the disbelievers that they denied (it).

﴿On the Day when﴾ (the verb is read both with the *yāʾ* (الياء), giving *yanfaʿu*, and with the *tāʾ* (التاء), giving *tanfaʿu*) ﴿their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers﴾, their excuse, even if they had offered one. ﴿And for them is the curse﴾, i.e., removal far from mercy. ﴿And for them is the evil abode﴾, the Hereafter, i.e., the severity of its punishment.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 53:

﴿And We certainly gave Moses the guidance﴾ (i.e., the Torah and the miracles) ﴿and caused the Children of Israel to inherit the Book﴾ (i.e., the Torah) ﴿after Moses﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 54:

﴿Guidance﴾ guiding; ﴿and a reminder for people of understanding﴾ a reminder for those possessing intellects.

﴿فاصْبِرْ﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿so be patient﴾. ﴿إنّ وعْد اللَّه﴾ with the victory of His allies ﴿is true﴾, and you and those among them who follow you [are included]. ﴿واسْتَغْفِرْ لِذَنْبِك﴾ [so that it may be made a precedent by you], ﴿وسَبِّحْ﴾ pray, being engaged in ﴿بِحَمْدِ رَبّك بِالعَشِيِّ﴾ [i.e., the afternoon], which is after the zawal (the decline of the sun from its zenith), ﴿والإبْكار﴾ [i.e., the dawn], meaning the five prayers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 56:

﴿Indeed, those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah﴾, the Qur'an, ﴿without authority﴾, without proof, ﴿having come to them. There is nothing in their breasts except greatness﴾, pride and ambition ﴿that they will surpass you﴾. ﴿They will never attain it, so seek refuge﴾ from their evil ﴿in Allah. Indeed, He is the Hearing﴾ of their statements, ﴿the Seeing﴾ of their conditions.

And it was revealed concerning those who denied the Resurrection.

﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth﴾ is the initiation, ﴿is greater than the creation of mankind﴾ a second time, which is the restoration. ﴿But most people﴾, that is, the disbelievers of Makkah, ﴿do not know﴾ this. So they are like the blind, and whoever knows it is like the one who sees.

﴿The blind and the seeing are not equal﴾: "لا" (here an extra particle, *zā'idah*, meaning it adds emphasis without changing the sense). ﴿Nor are those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾: this is the one who does good (*al-muhsin*). ﴿Nor the wrongdoer﴾: in it there is an extra "لا". ﴿Little do you take heed﴾: they are admonished, read with the *ya'* and the *ta'*. That is, their taking heed is very little indeed.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 59:

﴿Indeed, the Hour is surely coming, there is no doubt about it﴾ (i.e., no doubt) ﴿concerning it; but most people do not believe﴾ in it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 60:

﴿And your Lord says: "Call upon Me; I will respond to you."﴾ That is: worship Me, and I will reward you, by the indication of what follows it. ﴿Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell, humbled.﴾ It is read with a fatha on the ya' and a damma on the kha' (sayadkhulūna), and vice versa (sayudkhalūna). ﴿Humbled﴾ means abased, disgraced.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 61:

﴿Allah is He who made the night for you that you may rest therein, and the day giving sight. Indeed, Allah is full of bounty to mankind, but most of mankind do not give thanks.﴾ Ascribing the seeing (al-ibsar) to the day is metaphorical (majazi), because people see within it. ﴿Indeed, Allah is full of bounty to mankind, but most of mankind do not give thanks﴾ Allah, so they do not believe.
﴿That is Allah, your Lord, the Creator of all things. There is no deity except Him, so how are you turned away?﴾ How, then, are you turned away from faith when the proof is established?

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 63:

﴿Thus are they turned away﴾ i.e., like the deception of these people is the deception of ﴿those who used to deny the signs of Allah﴾ His miracles ﴿and reject them﴾
﴿Allah is He who made the earth a resting place for you, and the sky a building﴾ — a ceiling.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 65:

﴿He is the Ever-Living; there is no god but He, so call upon Him﴾ worship Him ﴿sincere in religion for Him﴾ free from association (shirk)

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 66:

﴿Say, "Indeed, I have been forbidden to worship those you invoke﴾ instead of ﴿Allah, [i.e., you worship]﴾ ﴿besides Allah, when there have come to me the clear proofs﴾ [i.e., the proofs of Tawhid (affirmation of God's oneness)]

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 67:

﴿It is He who created you from dust﴾ by the creation of your father Adam from it, ﴿then from a drop [of semen]﴾ (manī), ﴿then from a clinging clot﴾ (dam ghalīz, thick blood), ﴿then He brings you forth as infants﴾ (ṭiflan), meaning as children (aṭfālan), ﴿then﴾ He keeps you alive ﴿so that you may reach your maturity﴾ (ashuddakum), meaning the completion of your strength, from thirty years to forty, ﴿then so that you may become elders﴾ (shuyūkhan), read with a ḍamma and with a kasra on the shīn, ﴿and among you is he who dies before﴾ — that is, before the ashudd (maturity) and the state of old age. He did this with you ﴿so that you may live﴾ ﴿and reach a term appointed﴾, a specified time, ﴿and perhaps you will understand﴾ the proofs of monotheism, ﴿so that you may believe﴾.

﴿He is the One who gives life and causes death. So when He decrees a matter﴾, He intends the existence of a thing, ﴿He only says to it, "Be," and it is﴾. The verb ﴿فَيَكُون﴾ (fayakūn, "and it is") is read with a ḍamma on the nūn (fayakūnu) and with a fatḥa (fayakūna). With the fatḥa, the verb is in the subjunctive, with an implied ﴿أنْ﴾ (an, "that") before it, so the sense is "that it should be." With the ḍamma, the verb is in the indicative, so the sense is "and it is." Meaning: it comes into being immediately after the intention, which is the meaning of the saying mentioned above.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 69:

﴿Have you not seen those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah﴾ — the Qur'an — ﴿how﴾ (kayfa) ﴿they are turned away﴾ from faith?

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 70:

﴿Those who denied the Book﴾, the Qur'an, and they are the people of Makkah, ﴿and that with which We sent Our messengers﴾ of monotheism and resurrection, ﴿they will come to know﴾ the punishment for their denial.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 71:

﴿When the shackles are around their necks﴾, where *idh* (when) is in the sense of *idha* (when). ﴿And the chains﴾ is conjoined (*'atf*) to *al-aghlal* (the shackles), so that it is in the necks. Or it is a subject (*mubtada'*) whose predicate is omitted, meaning in their feet. Or its predicate is ﴿they are dragged﴾, meaning they are dragged with them.
﴿In the boiling water﴾, that is, Hell. ﴿Then in the Fire they are kindled﴾, that is, they are set alight.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 73:

﴿Then it will be said to them﴾ as a rebuke (tabkitan)

﴿besides Allah﴾, along with Him, and they are the idols. ﴿They will say, "They have strayed from us"﴾, meaning they have disappeared, ﴿so we see them not﴾. ﴿Rather, we did not used to call upon anything before﴾, meaning they denied worshipping them. Then they were brought forward. The Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell﴾, meaning its firewood. ﴿Thus﴾, meaning like the misguidance of these deniers.

It is also said to them: "That [punishment] is because you used to exult in the land without right" — [that is, because of] associating partners with God and denying the Resurrection — "and because you used to be insolent" — that is, you used to indulge excessively in exultation.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 76:

﴿Enter the gates of Hell, to abide therein forever; and wretched is the abode of the arrogant.﴾ (Translator's note: the commentary gives "مَأْوى" as the gloss for "مَثْوى", meaning "dwelling-place" or "abode".)

Note: "مَأْوى" (ma'wa, "shelter" or "dwelling") is the gloss the commentary gives for "مَثْوى" (mathwa).

﴿So be patient, for the promise of Allah﴾ concerning their punishment ﴿is true. Whether We show you﴾ — here إنْ is the conditional particle, assimilated (مُدْغَمَة, idgham, the merging of two identical or similar letters) with the extra particle ما, which reinforces the meaning of the condition at the beginning of the verb, while the nūn (the nūn of emphasis) reinforces its end ﴿some of what We promise them﴾ of punishment during your lifetime. The response to the condition is omitted, meaning: then that is so. ﴿Or We cause you to die﴾, i.e., before their punishment, ﴿then to Us they will be returned﴾, so We will punish them with the most severe punishment. Thus, the response that is mentioned belongs only to the conjoined clause.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 78:

﴿And We certainly sent messengers before you. Among them are those whom We have related to you, and among them are those whom We have not related to you.﴾ It is narrated that He, exalted is He, sent eight thousand prophets: four thousand prophets from the Children of Israel and four thousand from the rest of the people. ﴿And it was not for any messenger﴾ among them ﴿to bring a sign except by the permission of Allah.﴾ Because they are servants, subject to His lordship. ﴿So when the command of Allah comes﴾ with the descent of the punishment upon the disbelievers, ﴿judgment will be passed﴾ between the messengers and their deniers ﴿with truth, and the falsifiers will lose there.﴾ That is, the judgment and the loss became manifest to the people, and they had been losers at every time before that.
﴿Allah is He who made the cattle for you﴾. It was said: here the term refers specifically to camels, while the general sense (al-ẓāhir) includes cows and sheep.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 80:

﴿And for you therein are benefits﴾ from their milk, offspring, hair and wool, ﴿and that you may reach by them a need in your breasts﴾, which is carrying loads to towns, ﴿and upon them﴾ on land, ﴿and upon the ship﴾, the boats, at sea.

﴿And He shows you His signs﴾, meaning those that indicate His oneness. ﴿So which of Allah's signs will you deny?﴾ This is an interrogation (*istifham*) of rebuke (*tawbikh*) and reminder (*tadhkir*), meaning: "Which is more well known than its feminine form."

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 82:**

﴿Have they not travelled through the earth and seen how was the end of those before them? They were more numerous than them, and greater in strength, and in monuments upon the earth﴾ of *masani'* (structures, such as fortifications or large buildings) and *qusur* (palaces).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 83:

﴿When their messengers came to them with clear proofs﴾ the manifest miracles, ﴿they rejoiced﴾ that is, the disbelievers rejoiced with a rejoicing of mockery and laughter ﴿in what they had of knowledge﴾ that is, the messengers had of knowledge, ﴿denying it﴾ ﴿and there befell them﴾ came down upon them ﴿what they used to mock﴾ that is, the punishment.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 84:

﴿So when they saw Our might﴾ i.e., the severity of Our punishment

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 40, verse 85:

﴿So their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our punishment.﴾ ﴿It was God's way that has passed among His servants.﴾ Its case is that of a verbal noun (maṣdar), governed by a verb understood from its own wording: "God has made it a way (sunna) that has passed," namely among the nations, that faith does not benefit them at the time the punishment descends. ﴿And the disbelievers were lost there.﴾ Their loss became evident to everyone, though they had been losing at every time before that.
